$comment: FIRST WEEKLY READING after the baseline, same fixed query set, same order, same
transport (the owner's profiled Chrome). 10 queries, >=18s apart, no block.
HEADLINE: nothing moved. 9 of 10 carry an AI Overview, we are cited in none, and this
time we do not appear anywhere on the first page at all — the baseline had one organic
appearance at 2088px, which is gone. Against the baseline that is flat on citation and
one worse on presence.
THAT IS THE EXPECTED RESULT, NOT A DISAPPOINTMENT. Phase 2 shipped 2026-08-11, six days
before this reading. The design says the treated/control comparison is not readable for
4-12 weeks because it depends on a recrawl. A null at six days carries no information
about phase 2 either way, and reading it as failure would be the mistake.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEASURE: PR1 (JSON-LD entity graph), PR2 (copy that stops promising
the exact time) and PR3 (the per-city today hub) all landed on `dev` on 15-16 August and
are NOT in production. Google has never seen them. They cannot show up here until they
are promoted to master and recrawled.
THE ONE FINDING WORTH ACTING ON: alpenglowapp.com is cited in 2 of the 6 sun queries,
both times through /{locale}/times/{city} — the same family found on 2026-08-14. On
`a que hora amanece en tenerife` it is the ONLY source the overview cites. Four separate
queries across two sessions now point at that one page shape. Whatever earns the
citation, it is that template.
The vitamin D queries look structurally harder: their overviews cite health institutions
(medlineplus.gov, riojasalud.es, cun.es, contraelcancer.es) plus Instagram reels. That is
a different authority game from the sun-timing queries, and worth separating in analysis
rather than averaging the two territories together.
Method note: cited-ness is decided by links inside the overview block, and the block is
bounded by growing the label's ancestors past 150px — indicative, not exact. We verified
our own ABSENCE, which is a weaker claim to get wrong than presence. Domains are recorded
with their path this time, unlike the baseline, which stored hostnames only.

vsBaseline.note: The lost appearance was sun-nyc-sep, organic at 2088px on 08-10. One reading each way; the baseline itself recorded a query that flipped between consecutive days, so this is within observed day-to-day variance and is not evidence of a ranking loss.

observations.note: Still no overview at all, exactly as in the baseline. The stable counterexample.
Present organically at 2088px in the baseline, absent today.
The overview cites exactly ONE source, and it is alpenglow's times page.

competitors.$comment: Domains seen inside an overview's source box across the 9 overviews.
